The README (lines 152-154) says each re-derived operation sets the whole field 'to the v4 positive's value with the same edit', but the rule checks only key order, the unchanged keys, v4Refusal and the new refusal. findings.location: README.md 'The four T04 proofs' (lines 118-123); build_contract.py PROOFS
findings.finding: Two of the four proofs are not stated as obligations that T04 can close. T04-HOST-LOCKS requires the booleans and hardening settings to equal the record's 'for the whole enrolled boot'. But the enrolled boot itself sets them before the seal: one-way sysctls such as modules_disabled and kexec_load_disabled, yama ptrace_scope, and the booleans at policy load. A literal proof therefore cannot hold. T04-POLICY-STABLE says 'for the whole enrolled boot' and then narrows it to 'no policy load after the seal', so the window is stated two ways. T04-HOST-BOOT is anchored correctly ('for every capture of the record's window'). Coverage is otherwise complete: every dropped fact (the four host members; status and sequence, policy digest, booleans, every hardening member, the boot entry) falls under exactly one proof. The relation to the v4 record's t04Proofs is stated correctly: that constant is v4's ten (schema const, README:313-328).
findings.requiredChange: Anchor T04-POLICY-STABLE and T04-HOST-LOCKS at the seal, for example 'from the seal until the enrolled boot ends (so at every capture of the record's window)', and keep 'no policy load after the seal' as the content of T04-POLICY-STABLE. Regenerate the README and status hostProofs text accordingly.
